title: HPE patches eight max severity RCE and auth bypass AOS flaws
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise released security updates to fix 72 vulnerabilities in its Aruba network software, including eight maximum-severity flaws. These flaws could allow attackers to bypass login security or take control of affected systems.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Aruba network equipment, your IT team should handle these updates.
action_it: Apply HPE's security updates for ArubaOS to address the 72 patched vulnerabilities, including the eight maximum-severity flaws.

title: PHP Warns of Another Unpatched RCE Two Days After Emergency PHP2Shell Patches
summary: Hackers are actively trying to exploit critical flaws in PHP, a popular programming language used to build websites, while developers have warned of yet another potential issue. Because many websites need urgent updates, visitors may experience page errors or downtime while administrators apply security fixes.

also_covered.title: PHP2Shell Exploit Attempts Hit Millions as Attackers Try to Deploy Mirai Malware
Amazon says PHP2Shell exploitation began 4 days before patches
Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you run a personal website using PHP, you should check for software updates immediately.
action_it: Apply the emergency patches provided by PHP for the critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) immediately. For the newly disclosed issue (CVE-2026-115560), follow PHP's guidance to turn off the affected feature since no emergency patch is being issued.

title: Critical Flaw in Python’s Popular Pillow Image Library Allows Code Execution via a Crafted Image
summary: A critical security flaw in the popular Python image library Pillow allows attackers to run harmful commands on servers by manipulating image filenames. This happens because Pillow passes file names directly to another program without checking them first.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace or software development team uses the Pillow library, your IT and development teams need to update it.
action_it: Review applications using the Pillow library and apply updates or patches as soon as they are available from the vendor to address CVE-2026-112900.

title: Arista patches new VeloCloud Orchestrator zero-day exploited in attacks
summary: Arista patched a zero-day vulnerability in its VeloCloud Orchestrator that hackers are actively exploiting. This flaw allowed low-level users to gain full administrative control over the management system.

also_covered.title: Arista Warns of Critical VeloCloud SQL Injection Zero-Day Exploited in Attacks

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator, your IT team should already be on it.
action_it: Apply the security updates released by Arista for VeloCloud Orchestrator On-Prem deployments.

title: Researchers Demonstrate Node2Shell RCE Exploit on Node.js Build Using Crafted Brotli Data
summary: Security researchers demonstrated a method to run unauthorized code on Node.js using specially crafted data. This matters because it could allow attackers to take control of affected applications.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Node.js for software development, your engineering and IT teams should handle the updates.
action_it: Review Node.js deployments and apply vendor updates or patches related to CVE-2026-111497 as soon as they are available.

title: Critical x402 SDK Flaw Could Let Malicious APIs Drain AI Agents’ Token Balances
summary: A security flaw in x402 software development kits allowed malicious APIs to trick AI agents into draining their entire token balances. Security updates released on August 18 added spending limits to fix the issue.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you develop applications using AI agents, ensure your team is using the updated software.
action_it: Ensure that any applications using x402 SDKs are updated to the versions released on August 18 or later that include default spending limits.

title: Railway warns devs to rotate secrets after potential breach
summary: Cloud platform Railway warned developers to change their security credentials after detecting suspicious activity on systems storing customer data. This matters because attackers could potentially access sensitive passwords and keys stored in those accounts.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you use Railway for development, rotate all your secrets, API keys, and environment variables immediately as advised by the platform.
action_it: Instruct development teams to rotate all secrets and environment variables associated with Railway, and review access logs for any signs of unauthorized activity.

title: Capcom confirms data breach affecting 11.7 million accounts
summary: Gaming company Capcom suffered a data breach affecting its membership service, exposing over 11.7 million customer email addresses and related details. This matters because leaked email addresses and personal information can be used by scammers for phishing attacks or to guess passwords on other websites.
action_everyone: If you have a Capcom ID, you do not need to panic, but you should be on the lookout for suspicious emails pretending to be from Capcom. It is also a good idea to change your password on Capcom and any other sites where you used the same password.
action_it: IT and security teams should monitor user accounts for suspicious activity, alert affected users, and remind employees not to reuse personal passwords on corporate networks.

title: LiteLLM release pipeline hacked to distribute info-stealer malware
summary: Hackers compromised the LiteLLM software project to distribute malicious versions that steal passwords and sensitive data. This matters because anyone who downloaded the compromised packages or Docker images could have their credentials exposed to attackers.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace or organization uses LiteLLM, your IT team will need to investigate and secure any affected systems.
action_it: Review systems that downloaded recent LiteLLM packages or Docker images for signs of compromise, revoke any exposed credentials and environment variables, and update to a clean, verified version.

title: eMudhra to Exit Global SSL/TLS Business After 8 Intermediate CA Keys Found Easily Guessable
summary: Digital certificate provider eMudhra is exiting its global SSL/TLS certificate business after a researcher discovered that eight of its encryption keys were easily guessable. This is important because compromised keys could allow attackers to impersonate secure websites and intercept private data.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If you are an eMudhra customer, your provider should be replacing your affected certificate for free.
action_it: Review your certificate inventory to check if your organization uses eMudhra for SSL/TLS certificates, and work with the provider to replace any affected certificates immediately.

title: ThreatsDay: AI Secrets Leak, PingCAP Source Theft, Signal Hang-Up Flaw, Laravel Auth Bypass + 21 More
summary: A weekly cybersecurity roundup highlights multiple critical security issues, including PHP and GitLab flaws, Linux bugs, and compromised certificates. These diverse threats create a challenging week for security defenders across many different platforms.
action_everyone: Most people do not need to take immediate action, as these are a broad collection of technical threats affecting various systems. If you use any of the mentioned software or platforms at work, your IT department should review the latest security advisories.
action_it: Review the latest security advisories and apply available patches for PHP, GitLab, Linux, Node.js, and LiteLLM. Monitor networks and logs for any signs of compromise related to these recent threats.

title: Russian-Linked Hackers Used New Mesh Network Backdoor in Destructive Ukraine Attack
summary: State-sponsored hackers used a spear-phishing email to breach a Ukrainian logistics company last year. The attack deployed a new backdoor to help destroy data, showing ongoing cyber warfare threats.

title: Microsoft shares how to fix broken Exchange Online EWS apps
summary: Microsoft is explaining how IT workers can temporarily turn back on an old email service feature called EWS so that broken business apps work again. This matters because it gives organizations time to update their software before the feature is permanently removed.

title: The AI Agent Nobody Owns: Watch Expert Webinar On Your Newest Insider Threat
summary: Autonomous AI agents on corporate networks have access to sensitive credentials and internal systems with little oversight. This creates unmanaged security risks that resemble insider threats.

title: Machine speed attacks require machine speed detection and response
summary: Attackers can steal credentials and steal data within minutes, often beating human security teams. Automated tools are needed to detect and stop these fast-moving attacks immediately.
